# omw2mwse dry-run survey, 2026-11-27

*dej (dejunai). Generated by `scripts/survey_*.py`. Converter under test: omw2mwse 0.3.2 with omwcompat 0.4.4 (main b2a2790). Dry run only: nothing was converted, staged or deployed.*

## Method

- Sources: the repo test corpus (10 Nexus-sourced mods Dej downloaded earlier, plus Leave The Lights Off), every `modding-openmw` GitLab project with an `.omwscripts` file (57 repos, shallow clones of HEAD), GitHub repo searches (topics `openmw`, `openmw-lua`, `openmw-mod`, `morrowind`, name/description/readme queries, about 100 repos with an `.omwscripts`), six more GitLab/GitHub repos linked from modding-openmw.com, and the modding-openmw.com `openmw-lua` tag (241 mod pages, 190 of them Nexus-only; see below).
- Per repo: `omw2mwse --staged-root <repo> --result-json <f> --dry-run` (the tidy call) and `omw2mwse scan --json --no-installs --no-openmw <repo>`. Repos that hold several OpenMW mods give one verdict per mod (`mods[]`). Repos with several source folders (exit 2) were rerun once per folder with `--source`.
- Counted: 179 distinct mods. Not counted: OpenMW engine resource folders (`builtin`, `test_lua_api`, `morrowind_tests` inside engine forks), test/smoke/dump fixtures, engine forks and tools, repos with no active `.omwscripts` lines, mods with no Lua, and cross-repo duplicates (same mod name; Leave The Lights Off is counted once).
- Nexus mods cannot be downloaded without a login, so none were fetched. The 241 Lua-tagged mod pages on modding-openmw.com are listed in `docs/survey/nexus-candidates-not-surveyed.csv` for a manual round (only Dej can download those).
- Per-mod table with source URLs: `docs/survey/mods.csv`.

## Verdicts

| verdict | mods | share |
|---|---|---|
| ready | 19 | 11% |
| blocked | 160 | 89% |
| none | 0 | 0% |
| **total counted** | **179** | |

`none` is 0 because repos with no active `.omwscripts` lines or no Lua were left out of the count (a few; see mods.csv). Exit codes over 176 distinct inputs: 0 (ready/none) and 1 (blocked) as expected, 2 for the cases listed under "Exit 2", and no 70/64/3. No Python traceback appeared in any run or scan, so the converter never crashed.

Ready mods (19): morrowind_ai, TheGardenOfDreams, TheGardenOfDreams, m5_auto, BlockStealing, EssentialsKnockout, setbonus_rebalance, dynamic_morag_tong_armor, dynamic-telvanni-armor-replacer, harvest-lights-td-addon, harvest-lights, mage-robes-for-openmw-lua, momw-camera, MOMWModTemplate, shield-unequipper, LeaveTheLightsOff, NoFiresinBadWeather, wildlife_attacks_npc, fast_equip.

How far blocked mods are from ready (number of distinct gap families each needs): 1: 16, 2: 22, 3: 14, 4 or more: 108. So 16 mods are one family away, 38 are two or fewer away.

## Finding: manifest.json lags the runtime

`manifest.json` (what scan/convert gate on) still lists `openmw.animation` under `unsupportedModules`, has no entries for `I.AnimationController.*` and no `self.controls.*` writes, and describes `self.controls` writes as raising. The runtime has been quiet about all of these since 0.4.2/0.4.3. As a result 50 of the blocked mods carry an animation or `self.controls` blocker that the runtime would only warn about, and tidy would send them to `Off/<plugin>/OpenMW/` anyway. Only 1 would become ready from that fix alone (PetMudcrab), because almost all of them also need UI layouts, I.UI, menu or camera support. The same gate blocks Thieves Pickpocket 1.5.5 (the corpus copy) with 20 blockers, although a converted copy (built with 0.2.2) is in Dej's load order, so a fresh tidy run would send it to Off/.

## Exit 2 and crashes

No exit 70 (internal error), 64 or 3 and no tracebacks. Exit 2 (failed) occurred for these inputs; none is a converter bug, but several are things tidy will meet:

- **Several source folders** (`<Mod>: 2 different source folders ...; pick one with --source`): the call is all-or-nothing, so one mod folder holding a legacy copy or a second build cannot be converted without `--source`. Repro: `omw2mwse --staged-root <gitlab light-hotkey checkout> --result-json r.json --dry-run` (folders `.` and `legacy`). Also seen in pharis-magicka-regeneration, carefree_leveling (`0.48`, `0.49 or later`), Expedition32 (two patches), kinetic, and the four corpus mods that keep `_archive/full`. A relative `--source` is resolved against the current directory, not the staged root, and `--source .` scans the whole current directory.
- **Existing file not ours** (`conflict`): dev-chenxing/MyManor already ships `MyManor-metadata.toml` and an `MWSE/` folder next to its `.omwscripts` (a hybrid mod). Repro: dry-run on the checkout of https://github.com/dev-chenxing/MyManor. This is the guarded behaviour, but tidy should skip hybrids rather than offer `--adopt-existing`.
- **Every line commented out** (`no .omwscripts declarations found; nothing to host`): madsbuvi/openmw-lua-test-mods (`spellcast_mods.omwscripts` lines all start with `#`). Correct, but the message does not say the lines were commented out.
- **Case collision on Linux**: Tae410/Stance has `scripts/Stance/config.lua` and `scripts/stance/config.lua`; the converter reports `two source files map to scripts/stance/config.lua` (fine on a case-insensitive Windows tree, only appears here).
- Engine forks and their `builtin` mods (isowind, bru, openmw-enhanced, openmw-portal, Fetcher-Simulator) dry-run as 269-block mods; they were excluded from the counts.

## Recommendations for omwcompat

1. **Sync manifest.json with the runtime (cheap, do first).** Mark `openmw.animation`, `I.AnimationController.*` and all `self.controls.*` writes as stub/partial so scan and convert stop blocking on things the runtime already degrades. Alone it frees few mods, but it is also the gate that decides what tidy converts at all, and it is wrong today for Thieves Pickpocket.
2. **Magic read API (core.magic records and enums, Actor spells/activeSpells/activeEffects, selected spell).** Biggest non-UI gap: it blocks 67 mods and is the first greedy pick (+3 alone, more with others). Candidates to map onto in MWSE: `tes3.getMagicEffect`, the mobile `currentSpell` field, `activeMagicEffectList` and the object spell lists.
3. **I.UI mode functions (getMode/setMode/addMode/removeMode) and MENU settings-only scripts.** I.UI blocks 71 mods but is not HUD drawing; `getMode` is mostly "is a menu open", which `tes3ui.menuMode()` can answer. MENU is the second-widest blocker (67 mods) and the runtime already recognizes settings-only MENU scripts (0.4.1), so the scanner could host MENU scripts whose only calls are settings and `ui.showMessage`.
4. **Input handlers (`registerTrigger`/`registerTriggerHandler`, controller buttons, `onInputAction`, `onMouseWheel`)**, mapped to MWSE `keyDown`/`mouseWheel` events and the input controller. Blocks 52 mods; +2 to +3 alone.
5. **Skill and stat records (`core.stats.Skill/Attribute.records`, NPC races/classes, `I.SkillProgression`) and `I.ItemUsage.addHandlerForType`.** Each unlocks 2-3 mods on its own and the records are plain data reads.

UI layouts (`ui.create`, `ui.content`, `TYPE.*`, I.MWUI templates) remain the top blocker (85 mods) but the HUD/UI rule keeps them out; they appear only as a ceiling: no more than the in-scope numbers above can be reached without them. Camera (48) and `I.Combat` hit handlers (23) come next.

## Reproduce

```
python3 scripts/survey_run.py bin/omw2mwse <dir of clones> <out dir>   # dry-run + scan per repo
python3 scripts/survey_units.py                                         # builds units.json (paths set at top)
python3 scripts/survey_aggregate.py units.json agg                      # rankings, greedy order, manifest-lag view
python3 scripts/survey_report.py <survey dir> docs                      # this report and mods.csv
```
